biography.plain_text: Andrea Bocelli is an Italian tenor whose recordings and international concerts made him a leading figure in classical crossover music. Raised in rural Tuscany, he won the newcomers’ section at Sanremo before reaching international audiences with Romanza and Time to Say Goodbye, his duet with Sarah Brightman. His repertoire spans opera and popular song.

long_biography.plain_text:
Andrea Bocelli paid for singing lessons by performing in local venues while studying law, developing the voice that would become his profession. He trained with Luciano Bettarini and Franco Corelli, and earned a law degree at the University of Pisa. His operatic debut came as Macduff in Verdi’s Macbeth, followed by leading roles including Rodolfo in La bohème.

Through the Andrea Bocelli Foundation, established in 2011, the tenor and his family gave his charitable work a permanent organisation. Its projects in Italy and abroad address poverty, illiteracy and social exclusion. The foundation draws on relationships formed through his performing life to help people and communities overcome barriers to education and participation.

Andrea Bocelli paid for singing lessons by performing in local venues while studying law, developing the voice that would become his profession. He trained with Luciano Bettarini and Franco Corelli, and earned a law degree at the University of Pisa. His operatic debut came as Macduff in Verdi’s Macbeth, followed by leading roles including Rodolfo in La bohème.

Through the Andrea Bocelli Foundation, established in 2011, the tenor and his family gave his charitable work a permanent organisation. Its projects in Italy and abroad address poverty, illiteracy and social exclusion. The foundation draws on relationships formed through his performing life to help people and communities overcome barriers to education and participation.
